============================================================
**Jeni Neatherlin is the superintendent of Hutto Independent School District (Hutto ISD) for the 2025–2026 school year.** [1][1]

## Key Findings
The district's official website lists Jeni Neatherlin as Superintendent on its Executive Leadership Team and dedicated Superintendent pages, with detailed biography confirming her current role. [1][2] She was hired on August 27, 2024 (late 2024–25 year), ensuring she serves the majority of 2025–26 (Aug 2025–Jun 2026), with no evidence of transition or departure by February 2026. [6]

An older page mentions Dr. Raúl Peña (from September 2023), but current leadership pages supersede it per district site precedence. [4] Multiple sources, including 2024–25 org chart and 2025 articles, confirm Neatherlin. [3][7]

The district's official website (http://www.fpks.org) could not be accessed due to a fetch error, but state records take precedence when the site is unavailable, and no conflicting information was found across sources dated up to mid-2025. [1][8]

Based on my comprehensive search, the evidence strongly confirms that **Dr. Steven Caponegro** is the superintendent of Florham Park School District for the 2025–2026 school year. [4]

**Key Evidence:**
- The official NJ Department of Education 2023–24 District Detail report lists Dr. Steven Caponegro as superintendent. [4]
- Multiple current sources (ZoomInfo, Pursuit.us, updated January 2026) confirm him as Superintendent of Schools at Florham Park School District. 
- Wikipedia's entry on Florham Park School District (derived from public records) lists Steven Caponegro as superintendent with no contradictory information. 
- A January 14, 2025 NJ Department of Education Long-Range Facilities Plan amendment addressed to Dr. Caponegro confirms he was superintendent as of that date. 
- A 2019 article notes he began his superintendency at that time, consistent with a tenure approaching seven years without departure news. [7]
- No resignation, retirement, or transition announcements appear in recent news or official sources through February 2026.

The district website (http://www.fpks.org) could not be accessed during my search, but state government sources and multiple business directories consistently confirm Dr. Caponegro's continued tenure with no evidence of any leadership change during the 2025–2026 school year.

LEAID=2626430 | Oneida Township S/D #3, MICHIGAN | Step 1
============================================================
**Nate Lealy is the superintendent of Oneida Township S/D #3 for the majority of the 2025–2026 school year.** [4]

## District Context
Oneida Township S/D #3, also known as Strange School Elementary (a single-school district in Grand Ledge, MI), is served under Eaton RESA. The district's official website (http://www.eatonresa.org/our-districts/strange-school-elementary/) lacks a staff or leadership page listing a superintendent; it only provides contact details like email (strangeschool@gmail.com) and phone (517.627.7005). [8] A January 2024 Eaton RESA board brief noted plans to dissolve the district and transfer to Potterville Public Schools, but a May 2024 Eaton RESA ISD plan still lists it separately with Nate Lealy as District Superintendent, indicating continuity into 2024–25 and no reported changes for 2025–26. [9][4]

## Leadership Evidence
Nate Lealy signed the Eaton RESA special education plan as "District Superintendent, Oneida Township S/D #3" on January 31, 2024 (dated to 2024 approval). No evidence shows departure, transition, or replacement during 2025–26; Eaton RESA sites confirm ongoing services to the school into 2024–25 and 2025–26 without leadership changes. [4]

============================================================
**Sharon Newcom is the Director of Schools (superintendent equivalent) for Richard City Special School District for the 2025–2026 school year.** 

## District Confirmation
Richard City Special School District (also called Richard City School District), located at 1620 Hamilton Avenue, South Pittsburg, TN 37380 (NCES LEAID 4703540), operates Richard Hardy Memorial School as its single PK-12 school.[1]

## Leadership Details
Sharon Newcom holds the title "Director of Schools," the standard superintendent role for small Tennessee districts, as listed on the district's official website in faculty/staff and child find sections. Reggie Culpepper is titled Principal (sometimes listed alongside Newcom), handling school-level duties, but Newcom leads district administration.[10] Board minutes from May 2025 reference a "Superintendent Contract Renewal" approved for 4 years, aligning with Newcom's ongoing role into 2025-26.[8]

## Evidence Assessment
No district website mention of a superintendent transition, vacancy, or change during 2025–26; recent pages (e.g., 2026-dated board info) and minutes up to late 2025 consistently imply stability. GreatSchools and Child Find notices affirm Newcom's position as current.[10]

**Trish Newsom is the superintendent (titled Director of Schools) of Dayton City School (NCES LEAID 4700930) for the 2025–2026 school year.** [1][1]

## District Confirmation
Dayton City School is the official name for this single-school (K-8) regular public school district in Dayton, Tennessee (Rhea County), separate from Rhea County Schools; its address is 520 Cherry St, Dayton, TN 37321.[2]

## Leadership Details
The district's official website lists Trish Newsom as Director of Schools, the top administrative role, with 16 years at the district including prior positions as principal, counselor, and teacher; she was named Southeast Tennessee Regional Superintendent of the Year in September 2025.[1][2]  
In Tennessee municipal school districts like this one, "Director of Schools" is the standard equivalent title for superintendent. No evidence of transition, resignation, or change during 2025–26 (Aug 2025–Jun 2026); she served the majority of the year.[5]

No Montana state records (e.g., opi.mt.gov directories), news, or other sources name a superintendent or equivalent for this tiny rural district in 2025-2026. State superintendent lists (e.g., Big Horn, Blaine counties) skip Phillips County #1203 and show no matches for "Saco".

The older Arkansas Department of Education (ADE) data from 2023–24 also confirms Timothy W. Holicer as superintendent at that time. The ADE Data Center listing from December 2024 shows Chad Jordan E., and the Wikipedia entry (April 2025) lists Tim Holicer.

Given that the 2025–26 school year runs from August 2025 to June 2026, and the transition appears to have occurred in late September 2025 (after the school year began), the person serving the majority of the year would be the new superintendent introduced on September 24, 2025. However, the district website does not yet display the new superintendent's name—only Chad Jordan is listed.

Since the district website is presumed current and the staff directory page does not identify who the new superintendent is (despite the September 24 announcement), I cannot definitively name the new superintendent from available district website content alone.

============================================================
Based on the district's official website and supporting evidence, **Dr. James M. Pohl served as superintendent for the majority of the 2025–26 school year** (August 2025 – June 2026). [1][4] 

**Transition Timeline:**
- **June 11, 2025:** Dr. James M. Pohl appointed Interim Superintendent following the termination of Dr. Sharon Byrdsong. [4]
- **Early December 2025:** Dr. Jeff Rose's completed superintendent application submitted to Virginia Department of Education. 
- **December 2025 – January 2026:** VDOE completed certification reviews for Dr. Rose's application. 
- **February 23, 2026:** Dr. Rose's start date postponed due to VDOE licensure processing delay. 
- **February 26, 2026:** Dr. Rose appointed Acting Superintendent by special School Board vote due to VDOE administrative delays. [2]

Under the transition rule—since the superintendent transition occurred on February 26, 2026 (well after January 2026), Dr. Pohl, who served from June 2025 through February 26, 2026, served the substantial majority of the 2025–26 school year. [2][4]

============================================================
Perfect. I now have clear evidence of a transition. The SU76 administration pages show conflicting information:

- **www.su76.org/school-resources/administration/** (likely cached from late 2024): Lists "Mark Hurvitt" as Superintendent
- **sites.google.com/su76.org/** (current, undated but clearly updated): Lists "Tara Mckechnie" as Superintendent

Additional evidence:
- **April 13, 2025 Bangor Daily News article** [3]: Tara McKechnie was appointed superintendent of School Union 76 on April 11, 2025; Mark Hurvitt served "in an interim role since the resignation of embattled leader Dan Ross in December" (Dec 2024).
- **December 4, 2025 Sedgwick Select Board minutes** [6]: "T. McKechnie- SU76 Superintendent" attended a board meeting, confirming she held the superintendent title in December 2025.
- **Isle au Haut School Board page** : States "The Superintendent for School Union 76 and State Agent is Tara McKechnie" (undated but reflects current governance).

**Timeline:**
- December 2024: Dan Ross resigned; Mark Hurvitt became interim superintendent.
- April 11, 2025: Tara McKechnie was appointed superintendent of SU76.
- December 2025: McKechnie confirmed as superintendent in official meeting minutes.

**For the 2025–26 school year (Aug 2025 – Jun 2026):**
- August–December 2025 (5 months): Tara McKechnie served as the appointed superintendent.
- January–June 2026 (6 months, projected): Tara McKechnie continues as superintendent.
- **Majority: Tara McKechnie (6 of 11 months).**

However, by the TRANSITION RULE stated in the prompt: a transition occurred in April 2025 (before August 2025 start of school year). Since McKechnie's appointment in April 2025 is before the 2025–26 school year began, and she served from Aug 2025 onward, **Tara McKechnie is the superintendent who served the majority of the 2025–26 school year.**

Therefore, the person who served the majority of the 2025–26 school year (Aug 2025–Jun 2026) is **Alfonso Q. Llano Jr.**, who held the position from August through February 27, 2026 (approximately 7 months of the 10-month academic year). [3]

Per the instruction that "the district's own official website ALWAYS takes precedence," Llano's resignation date of **February 27, 2026** (published on vineland.org) supersedes any conflicting dates.  Roberto Euresti assumed the position **after** the majority of the school year had passed.
